title: observability: token/kv cost & latency advanced dashboard + alert tuning
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Context: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and KV-cache visibility have been a frequent ask from platform teams and a recurring signal in regression alerts (ENG-1421). This PR delivers a v2 of the token-cost/latency dashboard with KV cache metrics, enriched tracing spans, and tuned alert rules to reduce noisy paging.

Goals: 1) Surface per-route and per-model token cost and p50/p95/p99 latency so owners can correlate cost spikes with latency regressions. 2) Expose KV cache hit/miss rates and per-shard latency to assist runtime teams in tuning cache policies. 3) Reduce alert noise by adding adaptive thresholds, burn-rate windows, and recovery cooldowns. 4) Provide rollout-friendly dashboards and migration docs for teams using the legacy dashboard.

What changed: - New Grafana dashboard token_kv_cost_latency_v2.json with panels: token-cost-by-route, token-latency-distribution, kv-cache-hitratio, kv-cache-latency-by-shard, cost-per-token-heatmap. Panels include templating by model and region. - Prometheus rules: metrics/token_cost_latency.rules — aggregated histograms and derived cost_per_token metric (tokens * token_cost_rate). - Alert rules: observability/alerts/token_latency_slo.rules — added dynamic burn-rate alerts, noise suppression by container restart/scale events, and 10m/1h/6h evaluation windows. - Tracing: telemetry/tracing/span_enrichment.go — attach model_id, route_id, kv_hit boolean, and token_count to the response span for downstream correlations. - Metrics: observability/metrics/kv_cache.promql — kv cache hit/miss ratio and per-shard latency SLI. - Docs & examples: docs/observability/README.md and examples/console/token-level-cost-breakdown.md describe dashboards and migration steps. - Tests: tests/integration/observability_test.go adds synthetic traces/metrics to validate derived metrics and alert firing conditions. - CI: added grafana dashboard validation step and linting for rules.

Checklist:
- [x] Dashboard panels wired to consistent templating variables (model, region, route)
- [x] Derived cost metrics reviewed with finance (SUP-4123)
- [x] Alerts tuned to reduce noise from autoscaling events
- [x] Integration tests that simulate cache hit/miss scenarios
- [x] Docs for migration and rollback

Notes on risk and rollout: The change is read-only for production metrics ingestion and dashboards. The only runtime change is adding additional fields to tracing spans (model_id, route_id, kv_hit, token_count) which are safe and backward-compatible. We will roll out dashboards to staging, validate with a canary namespace for 48h, then promote to prod. Alert thresholds have initial conservative TTLs and will be iterated with on-call feedback.

Related: ENG-1421 (dashboard & alert priorities), ENG-1503 (kv cache observability), SUP-4123 (cost allocation).

Migration instructions: see docs/observability/README.md — includes JSON import steps for Grafana, Prometheus recording rule installation, and a SQL snippet to join billing allocations to route tags.

Release notes: token-level & KV cache observability improvements, new Grafana v2 dashboard, tuned alerts to reduce noisy pages and provide signal-rich correlations between cost and latency.
